reviews.author: Linus Torvalds
reviews.summary: Linus expressed enthusiasm for the patch and considered taking it as-is. He asked for comments, indicating a positive sentiment towards the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
On Tue, 10 Nov 2026 at 06:52, Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org> wrote:
>
>  11 files changed, 26 insertions(+), 360 deletions(-)

               Linus

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Zi Yan reviewed and approved the first two patches, indicating a positive sentiment towards the patch series.
reviews.raw_body:
On 10 Nov 2026, at 9:52, Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) wrote:

> pipe_to_sg() tries to steal the page of each pipe buffer and pass it to
> the host as it is.  When the steal fails, it copies the data into a page
> of its own.
>
> Pages written into the pipe with write(), gifted user pages and page
> cache pages can be stolen.  The ftrace ring buffer pages that
> virtio-trace splices cannot, so that in-tree user always gets the copy.
>
> Always copy.  The data that reaches the host does not change.
>
> Preparation for removing ->try_steal() from pipe buffers.
>
> Suggested-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>
> Signed-off-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>
> ---
>  drivers/char/virtio_console.c | 39 +++++++++++++----------------------
>  1 file changed, 14 insertions(+), 25 deletions(-)
>
LGTM.

Acked-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: Matthew Wilcox reviewed the first patch and suggested a code change, indicating a neutral sentiment towards the patch series.

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch series removes the pipe buffer stealing mechanism, which allows consumers to take pages from a pipe buffer instead of copying data. The mechanism is used by fuse and virtio_console, but it has been causing issues and is no longer necessary as both consumers can copy data when stealing fails. The patches replace the nosteal_pipe_buf_ops with default_pipe_buf_ops and remove the stealing mechanism.
